sources.detections: Global Fishing Watch public-global-sar-presence (Sentinel-1), non-commercial use
sources.imagery: Copernicus Sentinel-1 RTC via Microsoft Planetary Computer

coverage.note: Radar evidence covers only these 1-degree corridors, and only when Sentinel-1 imaged them.

detector.reference: GFW public-global-sar-presence detections (agreement, not ground truth)
detector.split: by Sentinel-1 scene (70/15/15 hash of scene id)

by_group.note: recall on positives of each group at the validation threshold

matching_summary.reference: GFW's own AIS match for the same IMO and day (agreement, not ground truth)

sts.reviewer: Claude (AI model) viewing 10 m Sentinel-1 crops; not an expert analyst
sts.rule: a second bright hull within 250 m of our matched tanker, or one target at least 70 m wide, at 10 m resolution
sts.wording: possible side-by-side activity; not evidence that cargo moved
sts.sampling: all two-target candidates and a random 60 of the wide-target candidates were reviewed

cargo_summary.labels: voyage context (weak): after a Russian export-terminal call = likely laden; before one = likely ballast
cargo_summary.decision: No-go: imagery did not clear the pre-registered gate. Cargo state stays UNKNOWN.

detector_review.reviewer: Claude (AI model) viewing 1.6 km Sentinel-1 chips at 10 m; not an expert analyst
detector_review.scope: every test-set disagreement between the CNN (validation threshold) and GFW

false_alarms.note: The 4 visible vessels are unreported by GFW (likely near-shore exclusions), i.e. label noise.

misses.note: Most misses show no vessel in the chip. Likely cause: two Sentinel-1 passes on the same date; the chip may come from the pass GFW did not use, or the ship moved.

detector_review.conclusion: Measured errors are dominated by reference noise; the agreement metric is kept as the headline and not re-scored by this review.
